text: A man of sense takes the time necessary for doing the thing he is about, well; and his haste to dispatch a business only appears by the continuity of his application to it: he pursues it with a cool steadiness, and finishes it before he begins any other.
author: Philip Stanhope, 4th Earl of Chesterfield
locator: Letter CXXIX, to his son, London, August 28, Old Style 1751
